contrast.text: No tracked sessions yet. Open a game's Profile setup to enable automatic restoration. Launcher submission alone does not create a session.
Found 1 game from Steam, Heroic, Lutris, Legendary and custom entries. Missing or unreadable store records are skipped.

A Flatpak game with a long descriptive name for setup and recovery
lutris/flatpak/1
Manual restore is selected. Enable automatic restore after choosing Performance or Quiet and setting up the wrapper below.

Automatic restore uses Power Profiles Daemon and a dedicated systemd user scope. It needs an enabled, authorized daemon, a user systemd session and a supported kernel. A canceled hold is never automatically reapplied. Other profile holds can change the effective profile.

Flatpak keeps the actual game inside its existing sandbox and resource limits. Install this launcher's helper, then copy the command into the game's launch settings. A blocked or canceled approval prevents that launch; it never silently runs without the requested hold.
Install the launcher helper, then put the wrapper command below in the game's launcher settings. Kernel/cgroup support and profile authorization are checked on each launch.
Use this as the game's Command prefix in Lutris System options. Keep existing required game arguments.

Removing this shared helper disables automatic restore for every game in this Flatpak launcher. Remove the command prefix from those games before launching again. Running games and their holds continue; Release profile hold ends a hold now. Sandbox permissions are managed separately in your desktop's Flatpak settings.
Setup check complete. Launch-time authorization and kernel checks still apply.
source: MOCK — fixture data, no real hardware
